Emergency shelters have opened across Reno, while a state of emergency has been declared in Washoe County. With hot and windy conditions expected to continue, the fire remains uncontained and residents face uncertainty over whether their homes have survived.

A landfill collapse in Conakry has killed at least 30 people, with many more still missing after heavy rains triggered landslides that buried homes built around the site's perimeter. Survivors describe a second wave of debris burying rescuers who rushed to help those trapped by the first collapse. Residents say they had long protested the landfill's presence and warned officials of the danger, accusing the government of ignoring repeated calls for its closure. Guinea's prime minister has visited the site, pledging resources for those affected.

author: Al Jazeera English
description: From fake celebrity endorsements to political disinformation and the rise of nudification apps, deep fakes are becoming increasingly common and harder to detect. In an interview with Al Jazeera, Sam Gregory, executive director of Witness and an expert on AI and synthetic media, warned that deep fakes are an "escalating problem" across three areas: consumer scams combining falsified voices and videos with celebrity likenesses; nudification apps creating fake sexual images; and political and conflict deep fakes that create "ambient uncertainty" about what is real. Gregory said detection is becoming increasingly difficult, with research showing people essentially fail to distinguish real from fake—"a coin toss" for audio and only one in five correctly identifying video deep fakes. He said the solution is not for individuals to stop sharing content online but to demand stronger enforcement, red lines, and new detection techniques from platforms. He noted that Meta allows nudification apps
title: Deepfakes are becoming harder to detect as AI scams and fake images spread: Analysis
